newsitem.title: USA: Ciller says Turkey won't cancel Iraq security zone.
newsitem.headline: Ciller says Turkey won't cancel Iraq security zone.

text.p: Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller denied on Monday that Ankara would be ready to cancel a security zone it has declared in northern Iraq if Baghdad acted against rebel PKK Turkish Kurds there.

"We are not ready to cancel the security zone because we fear the influx of refugees and the PKK has stationed themselves right next to our borders," she told reporters before meeting U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher.

The New York Times on Saturday quoted Ciller as saying in an interview that Turkey would be prepared to drop the security zone if Iraqi President Saddam Hussein was ready to "put an end to terrorist infiltration."

The remark, implying that Ankara might give Saddam a free hand in Western-protected northern Iraq after his military intervention there last month, was later denied in Ankara in a statement attributed to Ciller. She said on Monday it had been a "misunderstanding" with the Times.

The reported remark prompted concern in Washington that Turkey, a NATO ally that played an important role in the anti-Saddam coalition, was weakening in its backing of U.S. efforts to contain the Iraqi leader.
"We want to stop the influx of refugees through our borders but we cannot ask Saddam to do that for us because we have always respected the U.N. resolutions," Ciller said.

Ciller, in New York to attend the U.N. General Assembly, said the security zone, which would allow Turkish troops based inside Turkey to make strikes into northern Iraq against the PKK, "must be temporarily a danger zone."

Saddam restored at least indirect control of large areas of northern Iraq when he joined forces with the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) to attack a rival Kurdish faction and take the main northern Iraqi city of Arbil on Aug. 31.

Northern Iraq has been been protected from Saddam since the 1991 Gulf War by an allied air force based in Turkey that patrols the no-fly zone covering most of the Kurdish region. The United States responded to Saddam's interference with cruise missile attacks this month.
